name: Tuomo Suntola
summary: Finnish inventor of Atomic Layer Epitaxy (ALE), later renamed Atomic Layer Deposition (ALD). Led its development and commercialization from 1974 until stepping aside from active ALD work in early 1998.

name: Thor Stubb
summary: Professor at Helsinki University of Technology (HUT); ran the Electron Physics laboratory and later VTT Semiconductor Laboratory; Suntola's supervisor for his doctoral work.

name: Tapio Wiik
summary: Colleague of Suntola at VTT Semiconductor Laboratory; made the pre-study on the state of the art in humidity sensing.

name: Jorma Antson
summary: Worked with Suntola on the humidity sensor at Instrumentarium; completed the thin polymer film humidity sensor development in 1973.

name: Sven Lindfors
summary: Close co-worker of Suntola in ALE reactor design from 1975; demonstrated the ZnCl2/H2S process in 1978; later co-founded Picosun Oy in 2004.

name: Arto Pakkala
summary: Colleague on the ALE-EL team; reacted to the first successful ZnCl2+H2S run and helped switch chloride ALE-EL development to a new inert-gas reactor design.

name: Lauri Niinistö
summary: Professor of inorganic and analytical chemistry at HUT; provided scientific consultation on ALE chemistry and luminescent materials from the late 1970s; chaired the first International Symposium on Atomic Layer Epitaxy in 1990.

name: Jun-ichi Nishizawa
summary: Professor in Japan who investigated ALE growth of GaAs after the 1981 San Diego conference; initially renamed the technique 'Molecular Layer Epitaxy' (MLE) before recognizing it was the same technique as ALE.

name: Victor Drozd
summary: Invited Suntola to visit the University of Leningrad in 1990 to meet Professor Aleskovskii.

name: V. B. Aleskovskii
summary: Soviet scientist who, with S. I. Kol'tsov, independently discovered the essence of ALE in the 1960s under the name 'molecular layering' (ML).

name: Markku Leskelä
summary: Professor heading, with Mikko Ritala, the Finnish Centre of Excellence in Atomic Layer Deposition in the Laboratory of Inorganic Chemistry, University of Helsinki.

name: Mikko Ritala
summary: Professor co-heading the Finnish Centre of Excellence in Atomic Layer Deposition with Markku Leskelä.

name: Ahti Aintila
summary: Led the major developments on EL panel driving circuitries and associated manufacturing technology at Lohja; after 1984 founded Picopack Oy (1991) for smart cards using TAB technology.

name: Antti Piippo
summary: Business-oriented manager invited to Lohja's Display Electronics division; later bought Elcoteq Oy with close colleagues in 1991.

name: Matti Ervasti
summary: Business-oriented managing director invited in 1997 to take care of Microchemistry Ltd. and further ALE business development; Suntola's successor when he handed over Microchemistry in early 1998.

name: Kustaa Poutiainen
summary: Co-founded Picosun Oy with Sven Lindfors in 2004.

name: Pekka Soininen
summary: Started Beneq Oy's ALE reactor activity after the company was founded in 2005.

name: Tapio Alvesalo
summary: Head of Neste's venture team (Neste Advanced Power Systems, NAPS); saw the potential of applying ALE to manufacturing thin film solar panels and suggested the research activity that led to Microchemistry Ltd.

name: Jaakko Hyvärinen
summary: Constructed a fast solar simulator at Microchemistry to measure I-V characteristics of PV panels; later established Endeas Oy to produce 'Quicksun' simulators.

name: Marina Lindblad
summary: Doctoral researcher at Microchemistry Ltd.; completed a quantum chemical analysis of ZnS growth (with Prof. Tapani Pakkanen, University of Joensuu) as her 1992 doctoral thesis.

name: Salah Bedair
summary: Professor at North Carolina State University; his group demonstrated ALE of GaAs in a CVD system in the 1980s.

name: Stanley Myers
summary: President and CEO of SEMI (USA); presented Suntola with the European SEMI Award 2004 in Munich.

name: Ulf Ström
summary: Managing director of Finlux Inc., responsible for marketing ALE-EL panels in the USA.

name: Espoo, Finland
summary: Location of Otaniemi (HUT), Tapiola (Instrumentarium), and Olarinluoma (Lohja's EL production facility).

name: Lohja, Finland
summary: Site of Lohja Oy's Kunnarla TF-EL pilot production plant.

name: VTT Semiconductor Laboratory
summary: Established in 1964 as part of Prof. Thor Stubb's Electron Physics laboratory at HUT.

name: Helsinki University of Technology (HUT / TKK)
summary: Now Aalto University. Suntola studied and later did his doctoral work here.

name: Instrumentarium Oy
summary: Finnish medical instrumentation trading house; established a research group under Suntola in late 1973, within which ALE was invented in 1974.

name: Datex Oy
summary: Small technology company established by Instrumentarium; its key technical team, including Suntola, left the company in late 1973.

name: Vaisala Oy
summary: Finnish meteorological instrumentation company; VTT Semiconductor Laboratory's first industrial order (1971) was a humidity sensor for Vaisala. Vaisala's Humicap-based instruments remain the world market leader in humidity measurement.

name: Lohja Oy
summary: Bought the ALE-EL project, personnel, and facility from Instrumentarium in 1978; ran TF-EL pilot production from 1983 and the Olarinluoma production facility from 1985; sold its EL business to Planar Inc. in 1990.

name: Compagnie Générale d'Électricité (CGE)
summary: Big French state-owned company that licensed the ALE-EL technology from Lohja starting 1983.

name: Planar Inc.
summary: American EL manufacturer that bought Lohja's EL business in 1990, becoming Planar International; acquired by Beneq Oy in 2012.

name: Beneq Oy
summary: Founded in 2005 by Pekka Soininen, who started its ALE reactor activity; acquired Planar's Olarinluoma EL plant in 2012.

name: Neste Oy
summary: Finnish national oil company; its venture unit NAPS backed the founding of Microchemistry Ltd. in 1987; later merged with IVO to form Fortum Oyj.

name: Neste Advanced Power Systems (NAPS)
summary: Corporate venture unit of Neste Oy studying business possibilities in renewable energy; headed by Tapio Alvesalo.

name: Microchemistry Ltd.
summary: Subsidiary of Neste set up in 1987 for Suntola to develop ALE-based solar panels and, soon after, heterogeneous catalysis and ALE for semiconductor devices; sold to ASM in 1999.

name: ASM Microchemistry
summary: Name of Microchemistry's Finland-based ALE research activity after Microchemistry was sold to the Dutch company ASM in 1999.

name: Picosun Oy
summary: Founded in 2004 by Sven Lindfors and Kustaa Poutiainen; Suntola joined as scientific adviser (later board member from 2007).

name: Nippon Electric Company (NEC)
summary: Japanese company; demonstrated an InGaP-GaAs-InGaP superlattice using 11 ALE cycles, one of the most visible Japanese ALE results in the mid-1980s.

name: North Carolina State University
summary: Prof. Salah Bedair's group demonstrated ALE of GaAs in a CVD system here in the 1980s.

name: University of Southern California
summary: Prof. DenBaars's group demonstrated ALD of GaAs in an atmospheric MOCVD system.

name: Tampere University of Technology (TUT)
summary: Suntola was invited to give semiconductor physics lectures here in 1973 and was nominated as a docent; a small ALE-related III-V semiconductor research group formed here from 1975.

name: SEMI (Semiconductor Equipment and Materials International)
summary: US-based industry association; presented Suntola with the European SEMI Award 2004.

name: Finlux Inc.
summary: US company responsible for marketing the ALE-EL panels in the USA; Ulf Ström was its managing director.

name: Elcoteq Oy
summary: Spun off as an independent contract manufacturer from Lohja's microelectronics division in 1990/91; bought by Antti Piippo and colleagues in 1991; went bankrupt in 2011.

name: Laboratory of Inorganic Chemistry, University of Helsinki
summary: Home of the Finnish Centre of Excellence in Atomic Layer Deposition, headed by Markku Leskelä and Mikko Ritala.

name: Atomic Layer Epitaxy (ALE)
summary: Suntola's technique of supplying elements to a surface in an alternated, cyclic, self-saturating manner. Conceived in early June 1974; later renamed Atomic Layer Deposition (ALD).

name: Humicap humidity sensor
summary: Thin polymer film capacitive humidity sensor developed by Suntola and Jorma Antson, completed by the end of 1973; still (as of 2014) the basis of the world-leading Vaisala instruments.

name: 1974 ALE patent
summary: First international ALE patent; Finnish priority date 29 November 1974, granted in more than twenty countries including the USA, Japan, and the Soviet Union.

name: 1979 ALE patent (2nd)
summary: Second important ALE patent, Finnish priority 28 February 1979, protecting the inert gas reactor and basic processes for ALE-produced EL displays; mentioned compound reactants (H2S).

name: Liquid Crystal Display (LCD) color patent
summary: Suntola's patent, 'Method for generating electronically controllable color elements and color display based on the method', applied for in 1985 and granted in 1990.

name: F-120 reactor
summary: Quick, compact research reactor for photovoltaic (CdTe) development designed by Suntola and Sven Lindfors at Microchemistry; also became the first commercial ALD reactor.

name: F-450 reactor
summary: Reactor enabling ALD processing of silicon wafers and glass substrates up to 450 mm x 450 mm at Microchemistry.

name: F-1000 reactor
summary: Microchemistry Ltd. ALD reactor for coating big batches of 500 mm x 500 mm substrates.

name: ALE-EL thin film display
summary: Thin film electroluminescent flat panel display made using ALE-grown ZnS(Mn) and dielectric layers; first publicly disclosed at SID 1980.

name: European SEMI Award 2004
summary: 'Honoring the Pioneer in Atomic Layer Deposition Techniques ... that paved the way for the development of nanoscale semiconductor devices.'

name: The Dynamic Universe – toward a unified picture of physical reality
summary: Suntola's book on a holistic, unified picture of physical reality, 3rd edition published April 2011 by Physics Foundations Society.

name: The Short History of Science – or the long path to the union of metaphysics and empiricism
summary: Suntola's book, published September 2012 by Physics Foundations Society.
